$meta.method: static extraction from shipped CSS + JS bundles (no headed browser)

stack.css: Tailwind CSS v4.2.4 (banner comment in 31497ea371de0bbc.css) + CSS Modules
stack.cms: Sanity (GROQ queries + data-sanity presentation attributes inline in bundle)

rootSizingConvention.consequence: 1rem === 10px. Every size in the system is authored in rem where the numeral is the px value / 10 (e.g. 1.8rem = 18px, 6.4rem = 64px). Tailwind spacing tokens are named by their px value (--spacing-48 = 4.8rem = 48px).
rootSizingConvention.caveat: Tailwind v4's own built-in scales (--container-*, --blur-*) are still authored against the default 16px assumption, so e.g. --container-5xl:64rem renders as 640px here, not 1024px. Same for the `container` utility breakpoints (40rem/48rem/64rem/80rem/96rem = 400/480/640/800/960px) — they are effectively unused by the design.

color.$note: All colors are plain hex (no oklch anywhere in the stylesheet). 8-digit hex values are alpha variants of the two core neutrals. Declared inside `@layer theme { :host,:root { … } }`.

--color-earth-dark.role: primary ink; dark surface in dark theme

--color-sea.role: decorative pastel — blue (label chips, quote-card glow)

--color-mist.role: decorative pastel — pale blue (icon tile bg)

alphaRamps.$note: Two alpha ramps over the two core neutrals. `oatmeal-*` is taupe #f8edda over dark; `earth-*` is earth-dark #5d5146 over light.

--color-earth-60.note: NAMED 60 BUT IS ACTUALLY 0.8 ALPHA (cc) — inconsistency in the source

[data-theme=light].note: identical to :root EXCEPT --color-border drops from earth-20 (0.2) to earth-10 (0.1)

[data-theme=dark].note: no --color-header override; the nav keeps taupe in both themes. Dark theme is applied per-block via `data-theme="dark"` on the <section>, not globally — there is NO prefers-color-scheme query anywhere.

topSixByUsage.$method: count of `var(--color-X)` references in the shipped CSS + count of Tailwind color-utility hits (bg-/text-/border-/from-/via-/to-/fill-/ring-/shadow-) across the 4 rendered HTML documents (home, platform, skilled-nursing, about-us).

ranking.usage: all body + heading ink, dark-theme page background, dark button fill
page canvas, text on dark, `white` button variant surface
every hairline: nav pill border, block dividers, table rules, button outlines
secondary button fill (tan/25 → tan/50 on hover), quote-card rule
primary CTA fill and hover; the single brand-signal color
nav pill fill, alternating section surface, all translucent light overlays on dark

topSixByUsage.longTail: The 12 pastels (sea/mist/lake/orchid/blossom/plum/forest/sprout/meadow/coral/apricot/clay) are each referenced 1–2× in CSS: they exist as a CMS-selectable swatch set for icon tiles and label chips, plus meadow/coral as tick/cross semantics in the comparison table. They are deliberately rare — the page reads as a two-neutral system with one yellow accent.

body.role: body copy, UI, labels, buttons, nav, stat captions. Bold 700 is used ONLY inside rich text (.txt b, .txt strong) and comparison-table headers — never for headings.

display.foundry: Blaze Type (marketed as the "Season" family; the shipped cut is Season Mix)
display.role: every heading level (.display,.h1–.h6 and h1–h6 inside .txt), the AgendaCards watermark, the testimonial quote body, and HubSpot form headings. Only ONE weight ships (400) — the display face never goes bold; scale and the italic cut carry all the emphasis.
display.italicUsage: The italic is the 'premium' accent. It is applied through rich-text `em`/`<i>` inside headings (base rule: `h1 em,h1 i,…{font-style:inherit}` is overridden by `.txt em{font-style:italic}`), and is animated character-by-character in the HeroSummit typewriter (italic flips on 450ms AFTER the type-on finishes). Editors mark a phrase italic in Sanity and it renders in Season Mix Italic mid-sentence.

fonts.fallbackStrategy: next/font local faces with metric-override fallbacks (ascent/descent/line-gap/size-adjust) so the Arial and Times fallbacks occupy identical boxes — zero layout shift. `font-display:optional` means on a slow connection the fallback is kept for the whole page view rather than swapping.

scale.$note: Classes are applied directly (.h1, .b2, .label) and ALSO auto-applied to bare tags inside a `.txt` container that is not `.txt-post` — e.g. `:where(.txt:not(.txt-post)) h2`. Responsive variants exist as `.md:h1` etc. Only ONE breakpoint (768px) changes the scale, plus one lg:b3 exception at 1024px.

base.note: base rule groups h2,h3,h4 together at 3rem/120%

b2.usedBy: feature titles, accordion questions, stage titles

b3.usedBy: default body copy inside blocks; `.txt-post` (blog prose) shares this rule exactly

b4.usedBy: nav links, secondary/caption text, button label (regular size)

label.usedBy: the ONLY positive-tracking style in the system — step pills, cursor tooltips, tertiary button text. No uppercase transform is applied anywhere.
label.note: `.b4.md:b3` is a special composite rule: 1.8rem/145%/-.01em at md.

letterSpacingLadder.$note: Tracking tightens as size grows — the classic optical-sizing move that makes the display face feel engineered.

rules..txt a:hover (hover:hover): text-decoration-color:#0000  — the underline fades out rather than appearing on hover
rules.lists: .txt ul/ol { padding-left:2em; list-style-position:outside } ; ul=disc, ol=decimal ; .txt li+li { margin-top:var(--spacing-8) }
rules.tables: .txt table { border:var(--border); border-collapse:collapse; width:100% } ; td/th padding .7rem 1rem ; thead th font-weight:700
rules..txt-content-table: borderless variant — td/th padding var(--spacing-20), vertical rules via border-left on :not(:first-child), thead th font-weight:400
rules..txt-post flow: > * + * { margin-top:var(--spacing-24) } ; headings not:first-child get var(--spacing-48) ; media/quote/embed/stats/table blocks and their next sibling get var(--spacing-48)

scale.$note: Tailwind v4 `--spacing-N` tokens, N = px value. Available as gap-N, p-N, m-N, etc.

--spacing-margins.role: page side gutter; also used as a vertical rhythm value in several blocks

--spacing-gutter.role: grid column gap — note it SHRINKS at md, opposite of margins

layout.--vp-height: 100vh → 100dvh under @supports (height:100dvh); ALSO overwritten at runtime to window.visualViewport.height in px

--nav-height.role: height of the floating nav pill itself

--header-height.role: nav pill + its top offset; used to pad the first block

--banner-offset.value: 0px when no banner; otherwise max(0, bannerHeight - window.scrollY)px
--banner-offset.note: set on documentElement by JS; header is `top:var(--banner-offset,0px)` so it rides up as the banner scrolls away

zIndex.note: blocks additionally get an inline `style="z-index:N"` incrementing 1,2,3… in document order so later sections stack over earlier ones (needed for the sticky/scale hero effects).

container.note: `.wrap` is the only page container. Inner content then uses one of ~40 hard max-widths (see contentMaxWidths).

contentMaxWidths.$note: recurring measure caps, in rem (÷10 = px ×10)

breakpoints.$note: The CSS only ever branches at 3 widths. Tailwind's rem-based `container` variants (40/48/64/80/96rem) are generated but unused by the design.

jsMediaQueries.FeatureStages sticky: matchMedia(min-width:1024px) — below that the block degrades to a plain stacked list
jsMediaQueries.FeatureScroll parallax: matchMedia(min-width:768px) — parallax is OFF on mobile

radius.pill: rounded-[10rem] (100px) — every button; `rounded-full` for icon buttons, nav pill, step pills and avatars
radius.floatingHighlightCard: 0.7rem at lg, scaled down proportionally: calc(0.7rem*14.04/26) at base, calc(0.7rem*18/26) at md

border.usage: applied via `[border:var(--border)]` / `[border-left:var(--border)]` arbitrary properties rather than Tailwind border utilities, so the whole hairline (width+style+color) swaps with the theme in one token.
border.themedWidth: always 1px; only the color alpha changes (0.2 default / 0.1 light / oatmeal 0.15 dark)

shadow.$note: Shadows are RARE and always soft, warm and offset-down — never a generic black drop shadow. All are defined inline as Tailwind arbitrary values.
shadow.lgPanel: 0 2rem 4.8rem -1.2rem var(--color-earth-20)       — lg:shadow on a large panel
shadow.videoPlayGlow: 0 0 2rem 0.4rem rgba(255,255,255,0.05), 0 0 3.2rem 0.6rem rgba(255,255,255,0.05)  — the frosted play-button plate over video

filterBlur.note: when a texture VIDEO is playing
when only the still webp is used; wrapper is -inset-[6px] so the blur does not reveal edges

gradients.$note: There are NO decorative brand gradients in the stylesheet. Every gradient is one of three jobs: (a) fade media into the page, (b) legibility scrim over a photo, (c) the yellow text-highlight sweep.

implementationNotes: Set `html { font-size: 10px }` FIRST. Every value in this file assumes it. If you keep 16px, multiply every rem by 1.6.

The colour system is two neutrals (#5d5146 ink, #fef9ed canvas) + one accent (#f9f665). Everything else is an alpha ramp of those two neutrals. That is what makes it read as expensive — there is no third hue doing work.
Theme inversion is per-section (`data-theme="dark"` on the <section>), not per-page. There is no prefers-color-scheme handling at all.

Hairlines are a single token `--border: .1rem solid var(--color-border)` applied through arbitrary properties like `[border:var(--border)]`. That keeps 1px rules consistent and themeable in one place.
Headings only ever ship at weight 400 in a display serif; scale, tight negative tracking (down to -0.04em) and the italic cut carry all hierarchy. No bold headings anywhere.
The `label` class (+0.02em tracking, 12–14px) is the only widened style and is reserved for chips/pills/tertiary-button text.

Section rhythm comes from three tokens (section-padding-s/m/l) that step 3.2/4.8/6.4rem → 4.8/8/11.2rem at 768px, plus per-block-type overrides. Build the same: one block wrapper that sets --block-pt/--block-pad-bottom per type.
Grid gutter SHRINKS from 2rem to 1.2rem at md while page margins grow from 2rem to 4.8rem at lg — content gets denser while the page gets more air.
